Puzzle 1092 Consecutive integers of the same parity

Problems & Puzzles: Puzzles

Puzzle 1092 Consecutive integers of the same parity

JM Bergot sent the following nice puzzle:

33=3*11 and 33+3+11=47

35=5*7 and 35+5+7=47

329=7*47 and 329+7+47=383

341=11*31 and 341+11+31=383

Q1. Can you find a larger pair giving the same

prime result?
Q2. Is it possible for more than

two to give the same prime result?

During the week 25.30 June 2022, contributions came from Paul Cleary, Emmanuel Vantieghem, Jean-Marc Rebert, Gennady Gusev, Simon Cavegn, Giorgos Kalogeropoulos

***

Simon wrote:

I noticed the sum results that have many solutions are often one less than numbers in https://oeis.org/A015702/b015702.txt

To find a first example I used: 2^8 * 3^5 * 5^3 * 7^2 * 11 * 13 * 17 * 19 * 23 * 29 * 31 * 37 - 1 = 13464187271799263999 prime.

Here the first and last few lines. For all 2623 lines, see attached Puzzle1092_Q2.txt

10098140453849447997=3*3366046817949815999 and 10098140453849447997+3+3366046817949815999=13464187271799263999

12502459609527887987=13*961727662271375999 and 12502459609527887987+13+961727662271375999=13464187271799263999

12903179468807627977=23*561007802991635999 and 12903179468807627977+23+561007802991635999=13464187271799263999

..

13464187264460281021=3638178179*3700804799 and 13464187264460281021+3638178179+3700804799=13464187271799263999

13464187264460341061=3641889599*3697033339 and 13464187264460341061+3641889599+3697033339=13464187271799263999

13464187264460545981=3666482819*3672235199 and 13464187264460545981+3666482819+3672235199=13464187271799263999

An even larger solution for both Q1 and Q2: (file expires in 6 days): https://filebin.net/zfc7f3b8i3bjqt9h

Emmanuel wrote:

Looking at the examples given by Bergot, I restricted myself to odd semiprimes

(if even semiprimes would be involved, I think Bergot would have started with the pair {14, 15}, producing 23).

So, let m = p q be a semiprime, p, q being odd primes. Put f(m) = m + p + q.

I examined all semiprimes below 200000000.

Then, the smallest set of two semiprimes that have the same prime f-value is indeed {33, 35}.

The biggest pair I found is {179999637,199999595}, producing the prime 239999519.

There are 765267 smaller solutions, including many triplets, the smallest being {141, 155, 161}} producing 191

and the biggest is {171270717,190300795,199815833}, producing the prime 228360959.

There are also many quadruples, quintuples, ... and so on.

The biggest set of semiprimes with the same prime f-value is :

{129729595,142702549,144555827,149189017,150810629,152432233,153729497,153945703,154233973,154260179,154563413,154819979,154864519,154980317,155010007,155057509,155321273,155412847,155438989,155482519,155489353,155493223,155494477,155514389,155531869,155547929,155550709,155565227,155565973,155589433,155594917,155599699,155603783,155604613,155605819,155621017,155621897,155623213,155630557,155640757,155645977,155646553,155647243,155649959,155649997,155650207,155650219,155650549,155650567} (49 members).

All these semiprimes have f-value 155675519.

I could not resist the temptation to look for consecutive semiprimes (with the same parity) with the same prime f-value.

Here are those I found :

{33,35}, f-value : 47

{25019,25021}}, f-value : 25343

{205727,205729}}, f-value : 206639

{1887239,1887241}}, f-value : 1889999

{4632491,4632493}}, f-value : 4636799

{28475387,28475389}}, f-value : 28486079

{173112767,173112769}}, f-value : 173139119

{184865201,184865203}}, f-value : 184892399.

Jean-Marc wrote:

Q1. Larger pair giving the same prime result :

[332, 377] -> 419

351 = (3^3 * 13) and 351 + 3 * 3 + 13 = 373

352 = (2^5 * 11) and 352 + 2 * 5 + 11 = 373

[351, 352] -> 373

351 = (3^3 * 13) and 351 + 3 * 3 + 13 = 373

352 = (2^5 * 11) and 352 + 2 * 5 + 11 = 373

[14, 15] -> 23

14 = (2 * 7) and 14 + 2 + 7 = 23

15 = (3 * 5) and 15 + 3 + 5 = 23

[116, 135] -> 149

116 = (2^2 * 29) and 116 + 2 * 2 + 29 = 149

135 = (3^3 * 5) and 135 + 3 * 3 + 5 = 149

[1028, 1254] -> 1289

1028 = (2^2 * 257) and 1028 + 2 * 2 + 257 = 1289

1254 = (2 * 3 * 11 * 19) and 1254 + 2 + 3 + 11 + 19 = 1289

[10057, 10146] -> 10259

10057 = (89 * 113) and 10057 + 89 + 113 = 10259

10146 = (2 * 3 * 19 * 89) and 10146 + 2 + 3 + 19 + 89 = 10259

[100086, 101166] -> 102481

100086 = (2 * 3 * 7 * 2383) and 100086 + 2 + 3 + 7 + 2383 = 102481

101166 = (2 * 3 * 13 * 1297) and 101166 + 2 + 3 + 13 + 1297 = 102481

[1000148, 1249797] -> 1250189

1249797 = (3 * 23 * 59 * 307) and 1249797 + 3 + 23 + 59 + 307 = 1250189

[100000250, 100055333] -> 100057417

[1000000047, 1328224820] -> 1333333399

1000000047 = (3 * 333333349) and 1000000047 + 3 + 333333349 = 1333333399

1328224820 = (2^2 * 5 * 13 * 5108557) and 1328224820 + 2 * 2 + 5 + 13 + 5108557 = 1333333399

[10000000031, 11428566646] -> 11428571471

10000000031 = (7 * 1428571433) and 10000000031 + 7 + 1428571433 = 11428571471

11428566646 = (2 * 7^2 * 23 * 1583 * 3203) and 11428566646 + 2 + 7 * 2 + 23 + 1583 + 3203 = 11428571471

My method for finding these solutions is as follows using:-

A * B + C = Pt

The target Prime is Pt, we then list all primes up to the Sqr root of Pt, set these as Pi. Then,

A = Pi

B = (Pt - Pi)/(Pi + 1). Test if this is a prime if so we have a solution Then.

C = ((Pt - Pi)*Pi)/ (Pi + 1).

***

Giorgos wrote:
Q1: If we are searching for pairs of numbers with the same parity with any number of prime factors,
then the possible primes are:

47, 71, 89, 167, 239, 251, 331, 383, 419, 439, 491, 503, 503, 571, 587, 599, 599, 647, 659, 683, 683, 739, 787, 829, 1049, 1151, 1223, 1259, 1289, 1301, 1319, 1319, 1367, 1699...

e.g. the last number 1699 produces the following pair

1602 = 2*3*3*89 and 1602 + 2 + 3 + 3 + 89 = 1699

1666 = 2*7*7*17 and 1666 + 2 + 7 + 7 + 17 = 1699

If we don't care about parity, there are more ways to express these primes. For example, in Bergot's example we can also have

254 = 2*127 and 254 + 2 + 127 = 383

If we are searching for pairs of numbers with the same parity with exactly 2 prime factors (Semiprimes), then the possible primes are:
47, 71, 167, 251, 383, 503, 587, 599, 647, 683, 1151, 1223, 1259, 1319, 1367, 2099...

The largest prime that I could find that can be expressed in exactly 2 ways is 10^60+3439 :

999985469340308049985469340308049985469340308049985469274929 = 68819 * 14530659691950014530659691950014530659691950014530659691 and

999985469340308049985469340308049985469340308049985469274929 + 68819 + 14530659691950014530659691950014530659691950014530659691 = 10^60+3439

999999999999998814302835590138818580525657485842502606958483 = 843385672173479 * 1185697164409861181419474342513314111720871477 and

999999999999998814302835590138818580525657485842502606958483 + 843385672173479 + 1185697164409861181419474342513314111720871477 = 10^60+3439

It is pretty easy to find even bigger primes.

Q2. It is possible to find more than two numbers with the same parity that return the same prime result.

Here is a list of primes that can be expressed in k number of ways:

k number of ways | primes P

_______________|_____________________

3 -> 239

4 -> 359

7 -> 1439

8 -> 7919

9 -> 18719

10 -> 37799

12 -> 55439

13 -> 110879

15 -> 166319

18 -> 514079

19 -> 665279

23 -> 831599

. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .

168 -> 30561299999999999999999999

186 -> 52598699999999999999999999

199 -> 63617399999999999999999999

221 -> 79361099999999999999999999

and the list goes on...

One observation that helped me to easily find these primes is that their digitsum mod 9 is congruent to 8.

All these numbers that produce those primes in my examples are semiprimes.

So, the prime 79361099999999999999999999 can be expressed in 221 ways.

I'm sending you a txt file with all 221 numbers in the same format as the example of Bergot,

It is also easy to find bigger primes that can be expressed in more ways.
